title: Metallic Manhattan
descriptionHtml:
This is a screen printed interpretation of a large painting made to accompany the Radiohead LP 'Hail To The Thief'; part of a series of works based on rough maps of cities that featured, one way or another, in 'The War Against Terror' which was launched to mark the start of the new 21st century in an appropriately military fashion. Baghdad, of course, was subjected to an operation that would 'shock and awe' the city, which it doubtless did, along with killing, mutilating and psychologically maiming millions of people and laying the foundations for the emergence of ISIS.

8 colour screen print
Paper size 580mm x 640mm
Print size 500mm x 500mm
From an edition of 100

title: Capitol Meteorite
descriptionHtml:
In 2012 I completed an ambitious linocutting project; Lost Angeles, an eighteen-foot long panorama of the City of Angels being destroyed by fire, flood and a shower of deadly, flaming meteorites, all in a quasi-Mediaeval style, the Op-Art waves carrying the sad flotsam of the city. I worked on this linocut the the bright sunshine of California, aware all the time of the incredible fragility of our civilisation and how quickly it could be swept away; not just by a physical disaster but by a political, social or financial failure. The idea that we are living on borrowed time has gained horrible immediacy of late. Still, it's all good, right?
This screen print is adapted from a section of that original linocut, and shows the Capitol Records building on Hollywood and Vine. As well as some meteorites.

Paper size 805mm x 520mm

Print size 740mm x 415mm

title: Truth
descriptionHtml:
FAKE NEWS! It's become something of a cliché, don't you find? But it remains an undeniable fact that certain persons in positions of power do not need to burgle properties in the middle of the night. They do indeed have to get up in the morning to operate the reins of power. So I've made this little remonstration as a screen print. Maybe you could use it to decorate the crumbling walls of your post-nuclear holocaust dream home?
TRUE NEWS!

6 Colour Screenprint

Paper size: 660mm x 380mm
Print size: 600mm x 300mm

title: Glastonbury 2011
descriptionHtml:
The Glastonbury 2011 prints are now in, in full lithographic techno-colour. As you can see, above. As usual, the process of making the artwork has been a jagged trajectory veering from dread to despair, taking in self-aggrandizement and smugness on the way. Still, that's not really relevant, is it? No. The point is, I like it, and I very much hope that you will too.


Edition of 250

Print size 400mm x 480mm.

Paper size 490mm x 590mm


Signed by the artist.
Blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory seal.

title: Traurigkeit
descriptionHtml:
Dark skies and ruins are reflected in the still waters glimpsed from afar. Nothing stirs; no birds in the sky, none on the flat lake. A sense of waiting, or a sense of ending? These pictures are vaguely inspired by the work of Caspar David Friedrich, although they have no human figure, no allegorical allusion nor a spiritual dimension. They are simply a expression of melancholy.


Two colour hand-pulled screen print.
Edition of 99.
Print size 500mm x 500mm (approx).
Paper size 580mm x 600mm.
Numbered and signed by the artist.
Blind-embossed with the Slowly Downward Manufactory seal.

title: Tristesse
descriptionHtml:
A second exploration of wistful sorrow. Perhaps we are somewhere else, or perhaps decades have passed. This is an attempt to capture a feeling as transient and ethereal as the subject that inspired it, the dream of a landscape that was known once, but has been almost forgotten. Again, a sense of waiting, or a sense of ending?
